protocol.py: 2 biology problems (2 notes).

1. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 35 wells never mixed after the liquid from well E1 in slot 1, the
liquid from well F1 in slot 1 and the liquid from well G1 in slot 1 went in (7% of the well)
   line 63:  p300_multi.dispense(1, plate[f"A{i}"])
   At line 63 the robot added the liquid from well E1 in slot 1, the liquid from well F1 in
   slot 1 and the liquid from well G1 in slot 1 to wells C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8 and
   27 more in slot 3, which already held water, the liquid from well F1 in slot 1, the
   liquid from well E1 in slot 1, the liquid from well G1 in slot 1 and 1 more (this line
   did it 12 times). The addition was 7% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and
   the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their
   own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. If the plate is
   vortexed and spun down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes straight to the
   instrument, the wells are not what the protocol says they are.
   Affected: wells C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8 and 27 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8 and 27 more in slot 3 after line 63:
   `mix_after=(5, 12)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 12, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [687003bccc30]

2. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: Well E1 in slot 3 never mixed after the liquid from well E1 in slot
1 went in (25% of the well)
   line 69:  p300_multi.dispense(5, plate["A1"])  # dispense into the 2x4 block of destination wells
   At line 69 the robot added the liquid from well E1 in slot 1 to well E1 in slot 3, which
   already held the liquid from well F1 in slot 1, the liquid from well H1 in slot 1 and the
   liquid from well G1 in slot 1. The addition was 25% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with it that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   If the plate is vortexed and spun down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes
   straight to the instrument, the wells are not what the protocol says they are.
   Affected: well E1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix well E1 in slot 3 after line 69: `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or
   `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide

can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
